data.revised_prompt: The top-down spatial layout, scale, and framing of the quadcopter diagram in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The central rounded-rectangle body block in <Picture 1> is <Subject 2>. The four diagonal arm bars with circular motor hubs and large translucent rotor discs in <Picture 1> are <Subject 3>. The target image transforms the flat schematic diagram into an 8K photorealistic industrial design rendering of a cold-grey quadcopter viewed from a direct 90-degree overhead angle under soft 5500K lighting. <Subject 1> is fully preserved. <Subject 2> is partially preserved; its central position and footprint remain, while its flat grey shape changes into a streamlined carbon-fiber fuselage with detailed hardware. <Subject 3> is partially preserved; the positions, angles, and proportions of the arms, motor hubs, and rotor discs remain, while their flat geometric shapes change into realistic mechanical components and spinning propellers. <Subject 2> features a matte cold-grey woven carbon-fiber shell with sharp 60-degree beveled edges, a recessed anodized aluminum honeycomb grille along the center, a discreet flush-mounted GPS antenna module on the upper surface, and a glowing blue LED light band tracing the perimeter. <Subject 3> consists of foldable dark-grey carbon-fiber arms connected to the fuselage via metallic modular quick-release connectors, terminating in cylindrical reinforced dark-anodized motor covers at the four hub positions. Each motor cover supports two-blade ABS propellers coated with a subtle nano-coating sheen, captured in rapid rotation so the blades blend into the exact circular boundaries of the original rotor discs with faint motion blur and semi-transparent aerodynamic wash.
